name: LCW Mercury World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Founded with a fourteen-man single-elimination tournament in the promotion's own opening weeks, closed on a bloody "I Quit" match at Mercury Rising. Harbinger held it as the promotion's flagship champion into the winter, lost it to Pariah in a double-down shootfight the referee himself had to call, and Pariah carried it into Oblivion's own opening assault at Suicide, where Gol pinned him to become the group's first champion. Geoffrey Slate took it from Gol on an uncaptured show days later — the shortest reign in the belt's own short life, by the roster's own reckoning — and was still defending it when the surviving record runs out.

name: LCW Mercury North American Championship
notes: Called the "Platinum Title" once, in the federation's own December 2001 newsdesk recap of a card whose own results survive only in that basic-form summary (promotions/lcw-mercury/archive/mercury-front-page-2001-12.html); every other served document, including the federation's own champions.html and every show text from November 2001 forward, calls the same lineage the North American Championship. Recorded as a naming variant from a single dated source, not resolved either way.
epitaph: Founded to replace two retired belts in the promotion's own post-split reshuffle, and awarded to whoever climbed a bloodied ladder highest at Mercury Rising. Memosarks, Magnum Wolf and Geoffrey Slate traded it through the winter, Slate's own reign beginning with a cage-match escape at Silent Nightmare; Gol took it from Slate in the spring, and Dirge took it from Gol the week after, still holding it when the record runs out.

name: LCW Mercury Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Founded on the belts stripped from Evo's own Dean Wallace and Frank Heimdal in the split that made Mercury, and put up in a first-Fusion match the Trent Brothers won. The titles changed hands eight times across the promotion's own run — twice on Sloan's own turns, twice inside EEI's own shifting membership, once when Beaumont simply reassigned a vacated half without a match — before settling on Vincent Picasso and Johnny Glamour as the Elite, still champions when the record runs out.
